sentence: This project studies why lung cancer with a missing tumor suppressor is aggressive and resistant to treatment, and tries to target that cause.
This project tests whether radiation therapy works better against metastatic cancer when combined with agents that stimulate innate immunity.
This project provides statistical and computer support to researchers studying pancreatic cancer, including study design, databases, and data analysis.
This project tries to find out what makes abdominal aortic aneurysm get worse, looking at smooth muscle cell death and the aortic wall.
This project develops a method that makes large numbers of therapeutic nanovesicles from stem cells by extrusion.
This project develops and tests a brief personalized feedback session for people with HIV who drink hazardously and have negative affect symptoms.
This project studies genetic reasons some people stay resilient to Alzheimer's disease, with the aim of designing therapies that confer that resilience.
This project studies genes discovered to be linked to blood lipids and cardiovascular disease, using naturally-occurring genetic variants to learn what the genes do.
This project studies the clinical features, epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of enteropathogenic and enteroaggregative Escherichia coli infections in adults.
This project studies how transcription factors in the Hedgehog signaling pathway shape the pancreatic cancer microenvironment, including fibroblast and immune interactions.
This project builds artificial intelligence tools that combine facial images, clinical features, and genomic information to diagnose rare genetic diseases and uncover their mechanisms.
This project builds data science and research computing support for researchers, community colleges and state entities.
This project studies how histone demethylases control epigenetic remodeling in primordial germ cells, the precursors to sperm and egg.
This project studies how kainate receptors form a trans-synaptic junction and what this junction does for neuron function.
This project develops molecular imaging tools, including probes, instruments and assays, to diagnose cancer and check how well treatment works.
This project tests whether a story-based message delivered by digital and mobile technologies before wellness visits helps parents get cancer-preventing services for their children.
This project studies how opioids act in the brain to drive opioid use disorder, focusing on cortical neurons tied to their rewarding effects.
This project studies how to use T cells made from pluripotent stem cells as a ready source for cell therapies that attack tumor cells.
This project tries to find out why zebrafish regenerate retinal neurons after rapid acute damage but not after slow chronic damage.
This project studies the cell behaviors, genetic pathways and regulatory networks behind facial prominence fusion, which matters for cleft lip and cleft palate.
